title: Juan Pablo Montoya thinks he knows when Cadillac will reveal win-win Colton Herta plan for 2027
excerpt:
Juan Pablo Montoya thinks Cadillac would not lose “anything” by replacing Valtteri Bottas with Colton Herta for 2027, with the American now eligible for an FIA superlicence to race in F1.

There is a growing belief in the F1 paddock that Cadillac are putting the footwork in to hand Herta his debut in the pinnacle of motorsport at the expense of Bottas next year. Bottas has a contract with Cadillac for 2027, but his results so far in 2026 have raised doubts over his future.

Bottas and Sergio Perez both joined Cadillac to spearhead the American team’s debut season on the F1 grid in 2026 on multi-year contracts. However, while the latter has since secured an extension to his deal through 2029, Cadillac are believed to be weighing up releasing Bottas.

Juan Pablo Montoya tips Cadillac to confirm Colton Herta for 2027 at the 2026 Las Vegas GP

Behind closed doors, it is said that Cadillac privately call Bottas a contender for his own seat against Herta for 2027, which the team have further helped to fuel by now putting the latter in a position to earn his superlicence. Cadillac initially thought Herta driving in FP1 in Mexico City would move him to the 40-point threshold, but had to field him again in FP1 in Sao Paulo.

Herta had to hit the 40-point threshold needed to be eligible for an FIA superlicence required to race in F1 by the end of 2026 as he would otherwise lose the 30 points he got as the runner-up in the 2024 IndyCar standings. And taking part in FP1 at the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix has ensured that Herta is now on 40, and can apply for a superlicence to race for Cadillac in 2026.

Speaking ahead of FP1 at Interlagos, Montoya was already convinced that Cadillac will replace Bottas with Herta from 2027, too. The Colombian would also not be surprised to see Cadillac announce Herta as Perez’s next teammate at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix on November 19-21 to capitalise on revealing in the USA that the American driver will join the American team.

“If you look at the pace of the race, I really like Valtteri and all that, but Valtteri isn’t doing a good job; you’ve got to say it,” Montoya told AS. “And if you bring in Colton and Colton does the same job as Valtteri, you haven’t lost anything.

“But if Colton improves over the course of the year and closes the gap on Checo – because Checo is doing a brilliant job – and Colton can put pressure on him, that’s a win. Otherwise, they’ll end the year and look for someone else, which is exactly what they would have done with Valtteri; just find someone else, and that’s it.

“My opinion is that they’re going to use Las Vegas to announce it. That’s just me, I’ve made that up myself, but given it’s an American team in Las Vegas with an American driver, where would you announce it?

“This category is very complicated, the results are very complicated, and Colton comes from a different background, and every time he’s in Formula 1 – whatever race he enters – he goes very fast. So, I do believe – that’s my personal opinion – I believe that when they put Colton in the car, it’s going to be interesting.”

Herta left his position as a leading IndyCar driver to debut in Formula 2 this year in a bid to gain experience at certain rounds on the F1 calendar and with the Pirelli tyres, alongside serving as Cadillac’s development driver. And while Herta has “no interest” in returning to F2 in 2027 after struggling this year, he could now jump into a Formula 1 seat at Bottas’ expense.

Ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 F2 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, Herta has only scored 26 points to rank 19th in the standings out of 23 drivers. The 26-year-old’s best finish in Formula 2 to date also remains the P5 that he secured in the Sprint Race in Barcelona, when the Californian even ran wide at Turn 5 to blow his only chance to get on an F2 podium so far.

And yet Cadillac remain interested in offering Herta his F1 debut as Bottas has not been able to match the results that Perez has produced in the disappointing MAC-26. After 19/23 rounds of the 2026 F1 season, Perez leads Bottas 13-4 in their Grand Prix results head-to-head (having both retired in Austria and Hungary) and 11-8 in qualifying with an average margin of 0.235s.

Bottas has also not finished in front of Perez during a Grand Prix in which both Cadillac drivers took the chequered flag since the Chinese Grand Prix back in round two, either. The Finn took what remains Cadillac’s best result in F1 to date in Shanghai with P13, but has since finished behind Perez with both on the road in Japan, Miami, Britain, Italy, Azerbaijan and Singapore.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line Extra: Biggest 2027 Story at Team Penske? Climbing back into championship contention next season could help secure Josef Newgarden's (photo) future with Team Penske, one member of the Inside Line panel thinks.
excerpt:
Note: This series gathers the Inside Line panel to discuss the major storyline surrounding each NTT INDYCAR SERIES team entering the 2027 season. An installment on each team will appear at INDYCAR.com on Fridays.

Curt Cavin: See if this question sounds familiar: What is Josef Newgarden’s future with Roger Penske’s organization? It’s been a lingering topic, one that hasn’t had clarity due to the very private nature not only of Newgarden (photo, top) but also Team Penske. Yes, Newgarden is on a streak of 12 consecutive winning seasons – 10 in the No. 2 car – but he dealt with significant drama in 2025, and his two lowest season finishes with Team Penske have come in the past two years. The sport is better with Newgarden regularly challenging for race wins and the championship, and doing those things will go a long way to keeping him where deserves to be. Here’s my prediction for next season: Newgarden wins three races, including Indy, and signs a contract extension to make my contribution to this question seem silly.

Eric Smith: I’m looking at Team Penske as a whole and wondering whether it can reclaim its place not only as Chevrolet’s top team but as the top dog in the series. One could argue Penske was the fourth-best team in 2026, trailing champions Chip Ganassi Racing, Andretti Global, which produced the second-place points finisher and combined for three wins between Kyle Kirkwood and Marcus Ericsson, and Chevrolet rival Arrow McLaren, which placed two drivers in the top four in points and collected five combined victories. Three of Team Penske’s past five victories have come from Josef Newgarden on short ovals. Can Penske become a consistent threat across all track types? For the second consecutive season, the team won the season finale, but can its victory at Laguna Seca serve as a springboard toward a stronger overall campaign? Scott McLaughlin (photo, above) snapped a 35-race winless drought and finished 2026 as hot as anyone, putting together three consecutive top-five finishes. Newgarden, meanwhile, finished eighth in the standings. His last road course victory came at Road America in 2022. The two-time champion (2017 and 2019) will need to rediscover that form if Penske hopes to contend consistently beyond the ovals. David Malukas emerged as the team's highest-ranked driver, finishing fifth in the standings, but remains winless in his INDYCAR SERIES career.

Arni Sribhen: Team Penske isn’t used to being second to anyone, but they were second among Chevrolet teams in 2026 and fourth among all teams based on the results. The storyline for 2027 is a return to prominence for the team and improvement from all three of the team’s drivers. Three wins – two on ovals by Josef Newgarden – isn’t what Roger Penske expects. The pressure will be on the team’s leadership of Jonathan Diuguid (photo, above) and Travis Law to get the most out of Newgarden and Scott McLaughlin as well as upping the game of David Malukas in his second season with the team. Obviously, being healthy can only help, as both Newgarden and Malukas dealt with injuries that affected their performances during the season.

Paul Kelly: David Malukas surprised me with his performance during his first season with Team Penske in 2026. I did not think he would emerge as the highest points-earner in a lineup that also included two-time series champion Josef Newgarden and multiple race winner Scott McLaughlin. Can Malukas (photo, above) continue to prevail over his teammates in 2027? And will he emerge as a true championship contender for the entire season? There are two weak spots Malukas must fortify if he has a chance to lift the Astor Challenge Cup. One is obvious, and a fact I’m sure he’s sick of hearing: He must convert at least one or two of his four runner-up finishes from 2026 into victory in 2027. But he also needs better results on street circuits, as all six of his podium finishes last season came on ovals or road courses. His best street-race finish was sixth at Arlington, and he faded badly in concrete jungles at the end of the year, with finishes of 17th at Markham and 24th at Washington. Continued healing of his lingering wrist injury should help. But he must clean up his street-race performance to have any chance at a title.

title: 4 DAYS AGO •Driver News Five Drivers Who Helped Their Stock the Most in 2026
excerpt:
Like athletes in other sports, race car drivers have the chance to prove something each time they lower their helmet visor and drive out of their car’s pit box. The moment can come in a test, an official practice, qualifying or a race. Each is an audition.

In 2026, the performances of some drivers showed their current teams they were worthy of continued employment. Other drivers made compelling cases to opposing teams as well.

All the on-track results helped shape the 25-car grid for next season, with 15 drivers expected to remain with their current teams and 10 others taking new seats.

Some drivers helped themselves more than others. Here are five among the former:

Felix Rosenqvist

There is no overstating what a career-defining moment Rosenqvist (photo, above) produced on the last lap of this year’s Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

The Swede has always been highly regarded, and those who have worked with him have repeatedly praised him as a terrific teammate. But until May, his NTT INDYCAR SERIES highlight was a single race win in a 2020 doubleheader at Road America.

Rosenqvist not only parlayed his “500” victory into a signature moment in the event’s long history, but it almost certainly was the final piece to Arrow McLaren signing him away from Meyer Shank Racing.

In his new gig, Rosenqvist will work with fellow Indy 500 winners Scott Dixon and Ryan Hunter-Reay, plus two-time runner-up Pato O’Ward. The combination should give Arrow McLaren its best chance to return to Victory Lane at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

Christian Lundgaard

The Dane landed on his motorsport feet exceptionally well after Arrow McLaren chose not to retain him. But make no mistake: Lundgaard earned his way to Chip Ganassi Racing.

Lundgaard (photo, above) won two races this season, finishing second three times and third twice. He led eight races and finished third in the standings (one position ahead of teammate O’Ward).

Lundgaard still needs to prove he can win an oval race, but history is stocked with drivers of his ilk who needed time to excel on circle tracks. Perhaps Chip Ganassi’s organization can provide the information and the direction to do just that, and don’t sleep on the fact Lundgaard finished third and sixth in this year’s doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile.

It added up to a seat on a team that has won 18 championships in the 26 years since 1996, including six of the past seven with two different drivers (Dixon and Palou).

David Malukas

A show of hands please: Who had Malukas, in his first season with Team Penske, leading all Roger Penske drivers in points in 2026?

Malukas (photo, above) nearly became the driver to deliver Penske a record 21st Indy victory. The Chicago native was still ahead of Rosenqvist until the final few feet of the 200-lap event, finishing second by a scant .0233 of a second, the closest 1-2 margin in race history.

Malukas also finished second in two road course races (at IMS and Road America) and an oval race (Milwaukee).

Malukas began the year on a new multiyear contract, so perhaps he didn’t specifically improve his standing in 2026. But his confidence for next season and beyond has to be sky high.

Marcus Armstrong

It might seem odd for a driver who proclaimed his goal to finish in the top five – but finished 14th – to have helped himself in 2026. But Armstrong did, leading Indy coming to the white flag (photo, above) and leading by 4 seconds at Road America with five laps remaining before a mechanical failure cost him his first series victory.

Maybe it’s best to say Armstrong continued to help himself because Meyer Shank Racing didn’t make the decision to sign the New Zealander to a new contract and make him its lead driver for 2027 based on one season alone. But now he’s the team leader, replacing the departed Rosenqvist in the No. 60 car.

Second-year series driver Mick Schumacher will replace Armstrong in the team’s No. 66 car.

Marcus Ericsson

Ericsson (photo, top) went from 20th in the standings in 2025 to seventh this year, the largest jump by any driver in 2026.

But Ericsson did more than statistically improve – he won a race and solidified his spot at Andretti Global for another season.

Ericsson won the first Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham street race by recovering from a late pit stop to score his first victory since 2023. The win also was his first with Andretti Global.

By retaining his seat in Andretti Global’s No. 28 car, Ericsson is positioned along with Kyle Kirkwood and Will Power as the team makes a run at Chip Ganassi Racing’s spot as the best team in the INDYCAR SERIES.

title: 4 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line: Most Significant Offseason Development?
excerpt:
Today’s question: What is the most significant development of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES offseason so far?

Curt Cavin: I’m looking squarely at the supporting cast of Alex Palou’s No. 10 car. So much has changed recently within Chip Ganassi Racing, including the retirement of Julian Robertson (photo, above), who engineered all five of Palou’s NTT INDYCAR SERIES championships (and an integral part of the organization since 1993). Palou also won’t have the expertise of several other key personnel when the green flag drops in St. Petersburg, and it’s not inconsequential that he will be sharing information with Christian Lundgaard instead of Scott Dixon. (Palou still will have strategist Barry Wanser, which is a big plus.) But how all of this change comes together for Palou will be fascinating to watch, and if he wins another title next year it will be further proof that he’s the best driver of his generation.

Eric Smith: As I typically have done, I went outside the box here. Sometimes it’s not necessarily the move, but the moves not made that catch my eye. Chip Ganassi Racing and Arrow McLaren are amid a reshuffle of drivers and engineering lineups. Their biggest two threats for wins and championships are Team Penske (photo, above: from left: drivers David Malukas, Scott McLaughlin and Josef Newgarden) and Andretti Global. Both are running it back in 2027. In professional sports, teams talk about continuity and the advantages it poses. With two major organizations bringing back each of their driver trios and by all accounts keeping their pit stands status quo, I look for each to make another leap forward in 2027. Silence now could create noise later.

Arni Sribhen: For me, it’s the full-time return of Dreyer & Reinbold Racing. With the advent of INDYCAR’s charter system, many thought the NTT INDYCAR SERIES was a closed club with no way for any potential team to join the series. But the Indianapolis 500 stalwarts have done just that, even if it means starting from scratch. After purchasing its charter from Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing, Dreyer & Reinbold is back full time for 2027 with Conor Daly (photo, above) as its driver and a relationship with RLL as a Honda team. It will be interesting to see how the team builds in its return as a full-time team as it tries to finish the job started by the team’s late owner, Dennis Reinbold. The Reinbold family, especially Dennis and now his son Derek, has been loyal to the DRR crew since the team became an Indy 500-only team more than a decade ago. Many of the team’s core players, including team principal Chase Selman, have remained with the organization throughout. It would be a great tribute to see the team succeed.

Paul Kelly: This was a tough call for me between the return of INDYCAR SERIES racing to Europe with the Barcelona race in July 2027 or the continued testing of the IR-28 (photo, top) chassis. I’m choosing the new car. Alex Palou and Alexander Rossi have put the IR-28 through its paces on the smooth-as-glass Indianapolis Motor Speedway oval and the teeth-rattling bumps of the Sebring International Raceway short road course, about the two most diabolically opposite circuits one can image, since the season ended. And both tests went remarkably well, with both drivers able to turn ample laps with few to no problems. Sometimes I think we need to be reminded this is a brand-new car. It’s almost unheard of for a brand-new piece of technology to work this well out of the box. Development will continue in 2027, with all teams and drivers eventually taking the IR-28 for a spin, but the initial success bodes really well for a car that will look and race great starting in 2028.

title: 6 DAYS AGO •INDYCAR Technologies ECR Makes Major Investment in In-House Simulator Technology
excerpt:
INDYCAR Technologies

ECR will bring Driver-in-the-Loop simulation tools from Dynisma Ltd., a leading UK-based driving simulator technology company, into its team operation starting next season.

The team will be the first NTT INDYCAR SERIES team to use Dynisma’s race-proven DMG-1 Driver-in-the-Loop simulator. Scheduled for delivery in Indianapolis in the first quarter of 2027, the DMG-1 will provide ECR with dedicated high-fidelity simulation capability to support car development, race preparation and driver training across the wide range of circuit types that define INDYCAR competition.

ECR’s significant investment comes ahead of a major new chapter for the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. The all-new Dallara IR-28 will make its competitive debut at the start of the 2028 season, introducing a lighter chassis, revised aerodynamic concept and next-generation powertrain package designed to improve performance, drivability and wheel-to-wheel racing.

“We began exploring bringing a DiL in-house for over a year now,” said Ed Carpenter, ECR co-owner and CEO. “Simulation is something that we have committed to over the course of our team’s existence. After our visits with Dynisma, they became the obvious choice to move forward and bring this online prior to the introduction of the IR-28.

“Dynisma has a proven track record, and we are excited to be their first partner in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. Our drivers were very impressed with the capabilities of this product and look forward to having expanded access to the tool. ECR is on an upward trajectory toward achieving its championship aspirations, and this is just one step in that process.”

The new DMG-1 will give ECR a dedicated environment in which engineers and drivers can undertake repeatable development and preparation away from the circuit. Applications will include vehicle setup and dynamics development, driver familiarization, tire and balance optimization, race scenario rehearsal, engineering correlation and development of future vehicle models.

INDYCAR’s combination of high-speed ovals, short ovals, temporary street circuits and permanent road courses places uniquely varied demands on car and driver. High-fidelity Driver-in-the-Loop simulation enables teams to evaluate setup changes and prepare drivers for these differing environments before arriving at the circuit, maximizing productive engineering time when physical testing opportunities are limited.

Dynisma’s DMG-1 combines ultra-low motion latency of less than 5 milliseconds with primary motion bandwidth exceeding 50 Hz, providing the responsiveness and motion fidelity required for detailed vehicle development and driver preparation.

ECR driver Alexander Rossi has been the Chevrolet representative behind the wheel for all tests of the IR-28 so far, and he sees the immediate value of the DMG-1 simulator in that development of the existing and new car.

“At this level of racing, the smallest details make a difference, and the closer you can get the simulator to replicating what you actually experience in the car, the more valuable that tool becomes,” Rossi said. “What makes the Dynisma system particularly exciting is the level of responsiveness and feedback it can provide, which is critical when you're trying to understand the balance of the car and how it reacts to different changes.

“With the IR-28 coming in 2028, that becomes even more important. Having been involved in the development process, I know how significant the differences will be, and having a tool like this in-house will give us an opportunity to better understand the new car and accelerate that learning process before we ever get to the racetrack.”

title: Conor Daly, Dreyer & Reinbold Pass Key Test as Full-Time Return Looms
excerpt:
Dreyer & Reinbold Racing took another step toward its full-time return to NTT INDYCAR SERIES competition in 2027 with a successful road course test Monday, Oct. 26, at Barber Motorsports Park. It marked the team’s first time on a road course since 2020.

The outing marked an important milestone for the Indianapolis-based organization as it begins building the personnel, equipment and infrastructure needed to compete across the full 17-race INDYCAR SERIES schedule. Conor Daly, who was named the team's driver Sept. 5, drove the No. 24 Chevrolet around the 2.38-mile Alabama road course.

“Just getting there in the first place was a big deal,” Daly said. “There’s a lot of things we see in racing where people say we’re going to do this or we’re going to do that, but it doesn’t happen as easy as it sounds. It’s a great step forward to get there and to get on track with no issues and to just start logging laps. It’s a huge process and challenge that we’ve taken on.”

DRR announced July 22 that it had purchased an INDYCAR SERIES charter from Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing, setting the stage for its first full-time season since 2012. The team had continued to compete in the Indianapolis 500 every year since 2000.

However, returning to full-time competition represents a significant undertaking. The team last prepared a road-course car in 2020, when it contested three races on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. Its recent efforts have centered on the Indianapolis 500, making the transition to a full-season program an opportunity to rebuild and expand its operation.

Daly (photo, above), who has made 133 INDYCAR SERIES starts, emphasized the Barber test was about more than getting laps on track. While the team brings decades of Indianapolis 500 experience, expanding beyond May requires a different level of preparation and resources. The test marked the culmination of months of preparation and an important step forward for the organization.

“We’re all competitors on this team, everyone wants to do well,” Daly said. “We’ve seen so many times people want to enter this arena. It is not easy. It’s a tough sport to be involved in and jump into. I have so much I want to do in this series. This is a great deal to do it. To get going in 2027, to get on the grid and to get this process started is super proud.

“Great to see the smiles on people’s faces. There’s been a lot of work put in. To see it come through, to see it take place here on a road course, we’re not at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, this is a whole different world.”

DRR’s return to full-time competition came shortly after the passing of the team’s founder and owner, Dennis Reinbold, who died June 13 at 65. Derek Reinbold takes over as chief executive officer, leading the team his father established in 1999. The organization earned its first and only INDYCAR SERIES victory in 2000, when Robbie Buhl captured the season opener at Walt Disney World Speedway in the team’s debut.

Now, more than a decade after its last full-time campaign, testing allows the team to work toward another opportunity to compete throughout the season.

“It’s like first day of school, but it’s a new school,” Daly said. “It’s an awesome challenge for this group. Everyone’s been close to that point and excited to get there, and now we’re here. We’re not here to just be on the track.”

title: Frederik Vesti will have George Russell to thank if he denies Colton Herta a 2027 Cadillac F1 seat
excerpt:
Frederik Vesti’s FP1 session with Mercedes was extremely impressive and could help him push for a Cadillac seat.

There were 10 rookies on track during FP1 in Mexico, including Frederik Vesti driving George Russell’s Mercedes.

By the end of practice, Vesti finished in P3, just behind Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli. Cadillac rejected Vesti for a 2026 seat, but the Danish driver may have put himself back in contention for 2027.

How George Russell helped Frederik Vesti’s Cadillac push

It was Russell who sat out to allow Vesti to drive his Mercedes W17 in practice, and the British driver was pushing to help his colleague from the garage.

According to Motorsport Netherlands, Russell was urging Mercedes to allow Vesti to show his full pace in practice in order to help his Cadillac plea.

“The last thing George Russell said affects the driver market, because he also gave up his seat in the first free practice. 10 rookies were in the session, and one of them was Frederik Vesti.

“He got into the Mercedes and did very well with that third place. Then Russell said: ‘I gave a suggestion that, because Vesti has already done multiple sessions and had to work through the team’s programme, I asked the team if Vesti can do a performance run. So, low fuel, new tyres and then full throttle to show his potential.

“George said I really wanted that because Vesti is in the running to get the Cadillac seat in 2027.”

It seems Russell gave Mercedes the green light to give Vesti a full performance run in his car, dismissing any caution about causing damage or wrecking his weekend.

Frederik Vesti is competing with Colton Herta for Cadillac seat

Vesti’s pace in Mexico will catch the eye of F1 chiefs across the paddock, including the decision-makers at Cadillac.

But Vesti faces tough competition to secure a seat at Cadillac, including American driver Colton Herta.

Herta was also in action in Mexico FP1, and Cadillac have shown interest in bringing him in to replace Valtteri Bottas in 2027.

There are huge commercial benefits with Herta given that Cadillac have a large American audience and fanbase, so Vesti’s best chance of winning the battle for the seat is to prove he is a faster driver.

Russell certainly gave him a helping hand by telling Mercedes to take off the shackles while he was behind the wheel.

title: 2027 Driver Lineup Update: Few Empty Seats Remaining
excerpt:
The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES driver lineup is still taking shape.

Realistically, three seats need to be resolved by their respective teams, although officially there are four such seats open until Juncos Hollinger Racing confirms Rinus VeeKay’s expected return. The driver of the team’s second car also needs to be announced.

Dale Coyne Racing has not confirmed either of its drivers for next season. Earlier this week, the team tested INDY NXT by Firestone champion Nikita Johnson (photo, top) and Formula 2 race winner Alex Dunne at Barber Motorsports Park. Johnson, a Floridian, won two INDY NXT races in the recently completed season; Dunne, an Irishman, ranks third in F2’s standings with two races remaining.

AJ Foyt Racing resolved its No. 4 Chevrolet earlier this week by announcing INDY NXT race winner Josh Pierson. He will be paired with 2026 Rookie of the Year Dennis Hauger, the 2025 INDY NXT champion, who will drive the No. 14 entry.

The driver changes for 2027 are highlighted by six-time series champion Scott Dixon and reigning Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Felix Rosenqvist moving to Arrow McLaren. They take the place of Christian Lundgaard, who has replaced Dixon at Chip Ganassi Racing, and Nolan Siegel, who has not yet landed a seat for next year.

Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing will drop from three cars to two in 2027 after Dreyer & Reinbold Racing purchased one of its charters. DRR will be a full-season team for the first time since 2012, and it will do so with Conor Daly driving its Honda-powered car in a technical alliance with RLL (photo, above).

Overall, 10 of the 25 seats are changing hands, up from seven seat changes a year ago.

Mick Schumacher’s move from RLL to Meyer Shank Racing is the series’ other change. He will be paired with Marcus Armstrong, who recently signed a new contract and will move to the team’s No. 60 entry that Rosenqvist occupied each of the past three seasons.

One seat that hasn’t changed is the one the field again figures to be chasing. Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou will seek his series-record fifth consecutive season championship and sixth title in seven years. However, he will do so with a new engineer following the retirement of veteran Julian Robertson. Robertson’s successor has not yet been named.

The 2027 season begins Sunday, March 7 with the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg. All 17 races will air live on FOX.

A look at the 25-car field with new additions italicized:

CHEVROLET TEAMS

AJ Foyt Racing: Dennis Hauger, Josh Pierson (R)

Arrow McLaren: Pato O’Ward, Scott Dixon, Felix Rosenqvist

ECR: Alexander Rossi, Christian Rasmussen

Juncos Hollinger Racing: Rinus VeeKay, Second driver to be announced

Team Penske: Josef Newgarden, Scott McLaughlin, David Malukas

HONDA TEAMS

Andretti Global: Kyle Kirkwood, Marcus Ericsson, Will Power

Chip Ganassi Racing: Alex Palou, Christian Lundgaard, Kyffin Simpson

Dale Coyne Racing: Two drivers to be announced

Dreyer & Reinbold Racing: Conor Daly

Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian: Marcus Armstrong, Mick Schumacher

Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing: Graham Rahal, Louis Foster

title: The Ones That Got Away: Biggest Heartbreaks of 2026
excerpt:
In sports, there is the thrill of victory and the agony of defeat. It is the emotional essence of the games played, a reason why watching – and participating – is so enthralling.

That is, until one is on the latter end of it.

To paraphrase the legendary Bobby Unser, second-place finishers are generally remembered only by those who finish second.

In motorsports, there is usually a long list of competitors who share in such heartbreak, and the NTT INDYCAR SERIES generally has more than its share, particularly in the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge, which for every Al Unser Jr. there is a Scott Goodyear.

This year, five drivers finished the “500” within a second of earning a forever likeness on the iconic Borg-Warner Trophy, but four of those left Indianapolis Motor Speedway wondering what could have been. However, The Racing Capital of the World wasn’t the only site of heartbreaking moments – there were several this year. A look at a few of those instances, presented in the order in which they occurred.

Christian Rasmussen, Phoenix Raceway

A thrilling drive by the Ed Carpenter Racing driver throughout the Good Ranchers 250 effectively ended on Lap 207 with contact with Andretti Global’s Will Power.

Power was leading when Rasmussen (photo, above), the winner of last year’s race at the Milwaukee Mile, tried to pass on the outside in Turn 2. Their cars touched wheels, puncturing Power’s right rear tire and sending Rasmussen bouncing hard off the outside wall.

Rasmussen was able to continue with a compromised car, leading the rest of the lap and the 34 that followed, but he was eventually overtaken first by Andretti Global’s Kyle Kirkwood and then by Team Penske’s Josef Newgarden on Lap 242. Newgarden went on to win the race.

Rasmussen, who started 18th, led a career-high 69 laps but faded to 14th.

Power conceded he should have given Rasmussen more room, but the damage was done, and Rasmussen wasn’t happy about it.

“It’s just frustrating, man, so frustrating because we should have won the race and obviously didn’t,” he said.

Marcus Armstrong, Indianapolis 500

Coming to the white flag in the 110th Running at IMS, Armstrong could see his best opportunity to win his first series race – and the biggest of them all – but it wasn’t to be.

Team Penske’s David Malukas passed him on the outside as the field arrived at the flag stand for a one-lap shootout, and just as quickly Armstrong had Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian teammate Felix Rosenqvist alongside him in a duel for second.

Armstrong kept Rosenqvist on his outside for most of the final lap before being forced to lift in Turn 4. (Armstrong said his other option was to crash with his teammate, and the lack of another choice had him sour.)

Armstrong had the best view of Rosenqvist’s thrilling dart to Malukas’ outside in what became the closest finish in Indy history – a separation of .0233 of a second – but it wasn’t the view the New Zealander expected to see just a lap earlier.

“We were in position to win it, like that could have been us that passed Malukas,” Armstrong told FOX after admitting he had calmed down. “I can’t believe it, honestly – just so close. I feel I just made the wrong call at the most pivotal moment.”

To make matters worse for Armstrong, the rest of the sprint to the checkered flag became a three-way battle for third place, and he lost it to both Team Penske’s Scott McLaughlin and Arrow McLaren’s Pato O’Ward.

Finishing fifth never hurt so bad, although the strong run surely helped Armstrong’s cause for a contract extension that came about six weeks later.

David Malukas, Indianapolis 500

Malukas’ heartbreak was reminiscent of so many great drivers before him. Think Goodyear in 1992, Marco Andretti in 2006, O’Ward in 2024.

Malukas (photo, above) was ridiculously close to winning this sport’s biggest prize, running in front of Rosenqvist well past at the entrance to pit road for the final time. But as anyone who has ever walked the Speedway’s front straightaway knows, there is still a lot of ground to cover to reach the historic Yard of Bricks. Malukas learned that the hard way.

The two drivers finished the race side by side, but Malukas trailed by a distance of about half of a car length.

“I just don't know what else we could have done,” the first-year Team Penske driver said.

It was the third consecutive runner-up finish at IMS for Malukas, who followed Chip Ganassi Racing’s Alex Palou to the finish line of the “500” in 2025 and Arrow McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard to the end of this year’s Sonsio Grand Prix.

Indy was one of Malukas’ four second-place finishes during the season and pushed his career total of such finishes to six. Like Armstrong, he remains winless in the series.

Marcus Armstrong, Road America

Drivers positioned to win often have late-race mechanical issues, but Armstrong’s in the XPEL Grand Prix at Road America (photo, above) is highlighted here because he held a four-second lead with the laps winding down.

“You’ve got to be kidding me,” FOX broadcaster James Hinchcliffe said as smoke billowed from the back of Armstrong’s car four laps from the finish.

This disappointment was compounded by the fact he endured previous pain at Indy and he remained winless in the series in his fourth season. Lundgaard was the one to overtake him in this one.

“It was all smooth sailing,” a deflated Armstrong said. “I came out of Turn 6, and the engine just started sputtering like it was out of fuel. But clearly it wasn’t, and then it just completely died. There was no indication there was nothing wrong.”

Romain Grosjean, Markham

It might seem odd that a driver who finished second by 7.5305 seconds would fit in a “heartbreak” category, but Grosjean certainly did in the inaugural Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham (photo, top).

The French-Swiss driver moved atop the leaderboard with 21 laps remaining when Andretti Global’s Marcus Ericsson pitted for the final time. Ericsson, who dropped to sixth place with the stop, seemed to have fallen too deep in the pack to get back to the front in the competitive street race, opening the door for Grosjean to win the first series race of his career.

Grosjean drove masterfully and appeared to be poised to give Dale Coyne Racing its first victory since 2018 when Sebastien Bourdais won his second consecutive race in St. Petersburg. Grosjean finished the race with 28 laps led, but he needed five more.

With the laps winding down, Ericsson reeled in Grosjean, passing him on Lap 86 of 90. From there, the speedy Ericsson was gone, and Grosjean couldn’t do anything about it.

“I cried a little -- I'm not going to lie,” Grosjean said. “But control what you can control. I think that comes from (tennis legend) Andre Agassi … I did everything I could.”

The second-place finish was the sixth of Grosjean’s career.

title: Inside Line: Favorite Aspect of 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Schedule?
excerpt:
Today’s question: What is your favorite aspect of the full 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule that was released Oct. 23?

Curt Cavin: For me, the highlight of the 2026 schedule was the bang-bang-bang opening, and I’m happy to see that cadence repeated. For years, INDYCAR was a slow starter, with the 2024 season a perfect example: Six weeks between the first and second points-paying races. This year’s return to Phoenix Raceway (photo, top) made the early part of the schedule even better as the oval has long been my second-favorite track in series history (behind Indianapolis Motor Speedway, of course). This year’s schedule was rewarded with another stellar event in St. Petersburg, a thrilling return to Phoenix and a home-run debut in Arlington, Texas. I look for another great start to next season, and then it’s only a brief break until the fourth race (at Barber Motorsports Park). That’s hitting ‘em early.

Eric Smith: INDYCAR President Doug Boles talked Friday about how both drivers and teams are excited about the every-other-week race cadence beginning with the Fourth of July race at Mid-Ohio. While the final two race weekends are back-to-back, the stretch between Mid-Ohio and Milwaukee provides what Boles described as a great opportunity for the series to build momentum and promote each event. I like that approach. The breaks aren’t too long, but they provide enough time to spotlight the drivers and upcoming races while keeping everyone in the paddock fresh.

Arni Sribhen: The standout element of the full 2027 schedule is the historic addition of the inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya on July 18. This milestone event brings the NTT INDYCAR SERIES across the Atlantic for its first international race outside of North America since 2013, and securing a long-term agreement with the iconic Barcelona circuit gives American open-wheel racing a major global platform. Fan have been clamoring for INDYCAR get away from its Midwestern roots, and this race certainly does it.

Paul Kelly: While disappointed to lose an oval in Nashville, I still think the balance of the schedule needs to be praised. The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule is still the most varied, challenging lineup of tracks in global motorsport, with seven road-course races, five street-course races and five oval races. That mix tests drivers like no other series on Earth, especially in cars without power steering. I also like the cadence of the second half of the 2027 schedule much better than this year’s lineup. There are only two instances of consecutive race weekends after World Wide Technology Raceway (photo, above) on June 13, with no gaps larger than one off weekend. That’s easy for fans to follow, will create better racing and be easier on the crews than the final stretch of this season, when six races over five consecutive weekends left teams on fumes.

title: 2027 IMS Month of May Tickets On Sale Now
excerpt:
Track News

Tickets for marquee events in 2027 at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, including the 111th Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge and the Sonsio Grand Prix in the Month of May, are on sale at IMS.com and at the IMS Ticket Office.

The IMS Ticket Office is located on the first floor of the IMS Administration Building at 4790 W. 16th St. in Indianapolis. Hours of operation are 9 a.m.-5 p.m. ET Monday through Friday. Tickets also can be purchased by calling 317-492-6700.

Tickets for the following 2027 Month of May events are on sale at IMS.com and the Ticket Office:

Sonsio Grand Prix: Saturday, May 15

Miller Lite Carb Day: Friday, May 28

Legends Day: Saturday, May 29

111th Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge: Sunday, May 30

Indy 500 Coors Light Snake Pit: Sunday, May 30

Customers also can purchase admission to practice, qualifications and the Indianapolis 500 public drivers’ meeting, as well as parking, camping, hospitality and public credentials (Bronze Badge, Silver Badge, garage passes, pit passes) for these events at IMS.com. Fans also can purchase infield camping for the Sonsio Grand Prix.

“The momentum surrounding events at IMS, especially the Month of May, is spectacular,” Boles said. “Because so many fans renewed, we’re going on sale with limited inventory for the Indianapolis 500. Don’t wait to make your plans for 2027.”

All products are on sale at their lowest remaining prices, with increases coming in 2027. The $5 per-ticket service fee will be waived on items purchased before Jan. 4. Kids 15 and under will continue to be admitted free in general admission locations to all 2027 racing events at IMS when accompanied by an adult general admission ticketholder.

Month of May concert lineups, including performers and ticket sale information, will be announced soon.

title: Josh Pierson lands IndyCar ride with AJ Foyt Racing
excerpt:
Josh Pierson, an accomplished young American driver who has been a 2026 Indy NXT standout, signed a multiyear deal to compete in the IndyCar Series for AJ Foyt Racing starting in 2027, the team announced Tuesday.

"Racing in IndyCar has been my dream for as long as I can remember," said Pierson, who, at 16, became a Guinness World Records holder by becoming the youngest driver to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. "The variety of racing I've done has all been in preparation for this incredible opportunity."

Pierson's varied background includes local and international karting, junior formula racing, international sports cars and open-wheel competition in Indy NXT.

The 20-year-old has notched race wins and podium finishes in the World Endurance Championship, Asian Le Mans Series, IMSA and Indy NXT. This year, he started on the front row in each of the final three races of the Indy NXT season, including two pole positions, and at Milwaukee set a qualifying record previously held by new teammate Dennis Hauger.

Hauger will race in the No. 14 Chevrolet representing Homes For Our Troops, while Pierson will drive the No. 4 car with a sponsor to be named.

"I've been watching Josh closely for the past several seasons. Few drivers at his age have his depth of experience, and his maturity and work ethic are remarkable," said Larry Foyt, president of AJ Foyt Racing.

"Over the past year, he impressed us in multiple tests in a Panoz DP01 Champ Car alongside current IndyCar drivers, and again in our Chevy-powered car at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. I believe in Josh, and we're excited to be part of his continued development," Foyt added.

The FIA gold-rated driver acknowledged the history of the team he's joining. In 2027, it will commemorate the 50th anniversary of A.J. Foyt's historic fourth Indianapolis 500 victory.

"Being a part of AJ Foyt Racing, a team with incredible history, means the world to me. I'm excited about what Larry and the entire team are building for the future," Pierson said. "I'm grateful for their confidence in me and look forward to my first NTT IndyCar Series green flag at St. Pete."

title: Josh Pierson To Make INDYCAR SERIES Debut in 2027 With Foyt
excerpt:
INDY NXT by Firestone race winner Josh Pierson will make his NTT INDYCAR SERIES debut in 2027 after signing a multiyear agreement with AJ Foyt Racing, team officials announced Tuesday.

Pierson joins the team’s two-car lineup alongside 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES Rookie of the Year Dennis Hauger. Pierson will drive the No. 4 Chevrolet, with a new sponsor to be announced at a later date. Hauger was confirmed Sept. 16 as the driver of the No. 14 Chevrolet, which will carry sponsorship from Hendricks Holding Company.

“Racing in INDYCAR has been my dream for as long as I can remember,” Pierson said. “The variety of racing I’ve done has all been in preparation for this incredible opportunity. I’m grateful to everyone who has supported me along the way and tremendously appreciative of the commitment of a new partner that will be announced shortly.”

Pierson brings a diverse résumé to AJ Foyt Racing, with experience spanning karting, junior formula cars and international sports car competition. At 16, Pierson became the youngest driver to compete in the 24 Hours of Le Mans. Pierson has since recorded race wins and podium finishes in the FIA World Endurance Championship, Asian Le Mans Series and IMSA before returning to open-wheel racing in INDY NXT by Firestone.

The 20-year-old native of Portland, Oregon, made his INDY NXT debut in 2023, with his strongest championship result coming in 2025 with HMD Motorsports. He recorded two podium finishes and 11 top-10 results that season to finish sixth in the standings.

Pierson placed 11th in 2026, his first season with Andretti Global, while earning his first career victory in the INDYCAR development series by leading every lap from the pole at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. Pierson’s first pole last season came in late August at the Milwaukee Mile, where he set the two-lap average qualifying record.

The victory and poles capped a season with momentum, as Pierson also led the most laps and started on the front row in each of the last three races of the season.

That late-season surge followed a series of evaluations with AJ Foyt Racing, which tested Pierson (photo, above) multiple times over the past year. The sessions included testing the team’s Chevrolet-powered car on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course.

“I’ve been watching Josh closely for the past several seasons, AJ Foyt Racing President Larry Foyt said. “Few drivers at his age have his depth of experience, and his maturity and work ethic are remarkable. I believe in Josh, and we’re excited to be part of his continued development.”

Pierson joins AJ Foyt Racing ahead of a milestone season for the organization. The 2027 campaign marks the 50th anniversary of A.J. Foyt’s fourth Indianapolis 500 victory, which came in 1977. Foyt was the first among four drivers to win the Indy 500 four times. Al Unser, Rick Mears and Helio Castroneves later joined Foyt in the prestigious four-win club.

“Being a part of AJ Foyt Racing, a team with incredible history, means the world to me,” Pierson said. “I’m excited about what Larry and the entire team are building for the future. I’m grateful for their confidence in me and look forward to my first NTT INDYCAR SERIES green flag at St. Pete.”

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season starts Sunday, March 7 with the Firestone Grand Prix of St. Petersburg.

title: Nikita Johnson Savors Next Career Step With First INDYCAR SERIES Test
excerpt:
Nikita Johnson spent his teenage years working toward the NTT INDYCAR SERIES. On Oct. 26, the 18-year-old got his first taste of what it takes to compete at the sport’s highest level.

2026 INDY NXT by Firestone champion Johnson tested INDYCAR SERIES machinery at Barber Motorsports Park, sharing a Dale Coyne Racing entry with FIA Formula 2 standout Alex Dunne, who drove the car on the 2.3-mile Alabama road course during the morning session. Johnson took over in the afternoon. The test offered Johnson an opportunity to experience the physical demands of INDYCAR SERIES machinery as he looks toward the next chapter of his career in 2027.

“It was great,” Johnson said. “It was faster, more downforce. It was surreal. I watched this (series) forever. To finally be here was so special. It’s just everything I hoped for. More horsepower, more physical, more of everything. It’s just amazing.”

The St. Petersburg, Florida, native arrived fresh off an INDY NXT season in which he recorded two wins, eight podium finishes and 10 top-five results. He finished in the top 10 in all 17 races and completed every lap, the only driver in the field to accomplish those feats. Dunne entered the test third in the FIA Formula 2 standings after finishing fifth in the championship as a rookie last season.

Johnson’s championship came with an incentive package that could help him secure an INDYCAR SERIES opportunity for 2027, making Monday’s test a significant step in his development. He admitted he experienced some nerves as he waited for his turn in the car.

“I spent all morning waiting,” Johnson said. “How is this car going to act? How am I to compare it? To finally get in it, it was crazy to finally feel it.”

Barber was a fitting place for Johnson’s first experience in an INDYCAR SERIES car. He had four previous starts at the circuit, including a third- and fifth-place finish in USF Juniors in 2022 and a victory and a third-place result during his INDY NXT championship season.

“Great place to do it,” Johnson said. “Very happy to get it out of the system and just keep learning.”

There are adjustments to make, particularly under braking. The carbon brakes used in INDYCAR SERIES cars deliver a different level of stopping power than Johnson experienced in INDY NXT and the other junior series in which he has competed, which featured steel brakes.

“Everything was pretty spot on today,” Johnson said. “We did pretty well. Only little things I need to work on is the braking. I’ve got to get used to that stopping power.”

Johnson (photo, above) has made a career being able to make quick adjustments. He has established himself as one of the most successful young drivers in motorsports. Johnson earned three USF Juniors victories in 2022, followed by one USF2000 win and two USF Pro 2000 victories in 2023. After moving to USF Pro 2000 late that season, he won at Circuit of The Americas at age 15, becoming the youngest race winner in series history.

He finished runner-up in the USF2000 championship in 2023 and second in the USF Pro 2000 championship in 2024, when he won eight races. That same year, he added two victories in the GB3 Championship and became the youngest race winner in that series’ history with a victory at Zandvoort at age 16. He also won a race in Formula Regional Oceania in 2025.

Johnson last season became the youngest INDY NXT champion at 18 years, 3 months and 12 days old. His INDY NXT victory in the 2026 season opener at St. Petersburg also made him the second-youngest race winner in series history, at 17 years, 9 months.

If Johnson makes his NTT INDYCAR SERIES debut next season on the St. Petersburg streets on Sunday, March 7, he would be 18 years, 9 months and 13 days old. That allows him to join a select group of drivers who started a series race at 18 or younger.

Nelson Philippe holds the record as the youngest driver to start an INDYCAR SERIES race, at 17 years, 8 months and 25 days, when he competed April 18, 2004, at Long Beach. Graham Rahal is second youngest, having made his debut April 8, 2007, at Las Vegas, at 18 years, 3 months and 4 days. Andrew Ranger, Colton Herta and A.J. Foyt IV also made series starts at 18 or younger.

Herta remains the youngest race winner in series history, having won at Circuit of The Americas in 2019 at 18 years, 11 months and 25 days. Rahal and Marco Andretti are the only other drivers to win an INDYCAR SERIES race as teenagers.

Johnson has long had his sights set on reaching the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, with the goal of advancing through the ranks as quickly as possible. Monday’s test brought him one step closer to understanding what that next challenge will require.

“I always knew that I was going to try to fast track to get here,” Johnson said. “We always had the goal to be the youngest at everything. I knew I was going to be young, I just didn’t realize it was going to be this soon.”

Johnson takes the same approach for a potential NTT INDYCAR SERIES opportunity that carried him to an INDY NXT championship.

“Just one day at a time,” he said. “That’s what I thought about when I won my INDY NXT championship. Take it one day at a time and keep learning.”

title: Barcelona Is Ideal Spot for INDYCAR’s Latest International Event
excerpt:
The NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ return to Europe is more than a milestone on the calendar. It’s an opportunity for the series introduce its brand of high-speed, ultra-competitive racing to a new audience at one of the continent’s most recognizable motorsports venues.

The inaugural INDYCAR Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, July 18 at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya in Spain. The event was the centerpiece of Phase Two of the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES schedule. The multiyear agreement brings North America’s premier open-wheel racing series outside the continent for the first time since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the streets of São Paulo. It also marks INDYCAR’s first European race since 2007 at TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands.

“We are called frequently by international tracks and potential partners, and everybody's reported that from time to time we'll talk to somebody and just see what's out there,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “But then we got a call from Barcelona.”

The renowned road course that opened in 1991 has hosted Formula One and MotoGP events. Miles views this as an opportunity that could offer an established motorsports setting that will showcase the NTT INDYCAR SERIES while providing a strong foundation for a successful long-term partnership.

“This is an iconic track,” Miles said. “It’s the highest-level, highest-quality track, and we really got to know quickly the personnel, the executive staff, the governmental entities that look over the ownership of the track and believe these were people we could do business with. So, it just seemed like it's been four-ish months of work and discussions, but we felt like we could get here. And once we can be here, we think this is going to be a great home for the INDYCAR SERIES for many years to come.”

The announcement also carries a significance for Alex Palou that extends well beyond the championship implications of another race weekend. The 29-year-old Barcelona native captured his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship in 2026, becoming just the second driver in series history to win four consecutive titles, joining Sébastien Bourdais, who accomplished the feat from 2004-07. With five championships in six years and 25 career victories, Palou is tied for 17th on the series’ all-time wins list. Only A.J. Foyt, with seven titles, and Scott Dixon, with six, have won more championships. He now will compete in front of his home fans in an INDYCAR SERIES race that once seemed unimaginable.

“Incredible for me,” Palou said. “I never thought that there would be any day that INDYCAR would come to Barcelona. I dreamed about having the series go overseas and kind of going to Europe but never in my times and in Barcelona.

“It’s just a start, but I feel like everybody's super excited here. It's not like we're going to a place where they're not excited about INDYCAR or it's just another event for them. It will be the event next year here. Everybody's super pumped.

“I cannot thank the INDYCAR team enough for making this happen, the Barcelona team for making this happen. I'm just like a passenger here, and I'm just going to enjoy every single moment.”

Palou, who is the only Spaniard in the INDYCAR SERIES field, doesn’t believe he has to carry the burden of lifting an entire series through a country. He explained there are plenty of European drivers competing in the series, and Barcelona could provide an accessible destination for fans who have followed those drivers from afar but have never had the opportunity to see the series race on their home continent.

“It’ll be my hometown race, but it'll be the home race for more than 10 drivers that are from Europe, and they are only a couple hours away from here,” Palou said. “Hopefully, we get a lot of fans. We get a lot of new fans that they then get following all our schedule.”

The July race isn’t a one-year opportunity. The 2027 race weekend is the start of what both sides view as a potentially decade-long partnership, Miles said.

“This could be the home base for INDYCAR in Europe,” Miles said. “I think we're landing in the right place.”
